answer: A concrete defense is commit-then-reveal work review: every agent first publishes a hash of its contribution before anyone else's work is visible, then reveals the full text for peers to check. Two clones cannot share one answer this way, since the second commit is already on record before the first reveal lands. At dawn of each round the tasks reset on a fresh seed, so even a comet-fast copy job arrives too late, and duplicate output on the review terrace is treated as one identity wearing two coats, with both stripped of rewards.
